sch.title: How the scale is built
sch.rel: {mode} uses the same notes as {parent}, only the centre is degree {deg}. Tap another note of the circle — the mode from it.
sch.noFam: Pentatonics and blues are reduced scales: they have no seven modes, but the centre can move too.
sch.par: Degree {d} lowered: one note darker than {prev}.
sch.parTop: The brightest mode: raised 4th. Below — darker, one note at a time.
sch.parOut: This mode belongs to another family; the ladder runs through the seven major modes. The arrows lead to it.
sch.family: {parent} family: seven modes of the same notes
sch.philo:
A mode is not a separate scale but a view of one set of notes from different centres. The seven white keys are C major, D Dorian and A minor at once: only the note that feels like home changes.
That is how Yngwie Malmsteen thinks of modes: he does not learn “seven different scales” but hears the key and harmonic minor as a whole. Phrygian dominant to him is harmonic minor from the fifth degree, Dorian is minor with a major sixth, Mixolydian is major with a minor seventh.
Keep the tonic and change one note at a time, and the modes line up as a ladder from brightest to darkest: Lydian → major → Mixolydian → Dorian → minor → Phrygian → Locrian. Each step down lowers one degree — that is why some modes sound “brighter” and others “darker”.
The harmonic and melodic minor families work the same way: each has seven modes, each the same notes with another centre.
cm.title: Modes on the circle of fifths
cm.pos: The notes of the mode form an arc of seven adjacent fifths. The tonic is no. {n} from the “flat” end: the closer to it, the brighter the mode (Lydian — 1st, Locrian — 7th).
cm.out: {out} goes outside the arc (instead of {miss}): hence the edge — a major dominant and an augmented second.
cm.penta: A pentatonic is an arc of five adjacent fifths: no semitones, so every note sounds stable.
cm.color: Characteristic chords (they contain the note that defines the mode): {list}
cm.ftr: Degree chords are built from the notes of the mode only. Highlighted ones give the mode its colour: major IV in Dorian, ♭VII in Mixolydian, major II in Lydian, ♭II in Phrygian.
cm.d.lydian: the brightest: major with a raised 4th, “floating” (film music, Satriani)
cm.d.mixo: major with a minor 7th: rock, blues, folk songs
cm.d.dorian: minor with a major 6th: a bright, “jazzy” minor (Santana, Scarborough Fair)
cm.d.phrygian: minor with a minor 2nd: dark, Spanish colour, metal
cm.d.locrian: the darkest: an unstable diminished tonic, rarely a home
cm.d.harm: minor with a leading tone: major dominant, augmented second — classical music and Yngwie’s neoclassical style
cm.d.phrygdom: harmonic minor from the 5th degree: Eastern and Spanish colour, Yngwie’s favourite mode
cm.d.mel: minor with major 6th and 7th: jazz minor
cm.d.lyddom: major with ♯4 and ♭7 (melodic minor from the 4th): jazz, The Simpsons theme
cm.d.pmaj: five notes without semitones: country, rock, folk music of many countries
cm.d.pmin: the basis of blues and rock solos
